## 4. The recovery repairs — this session's own catches (the record, honestly)

This session is itself a recovery landing (the previous session died
mid-flight). Its live verification found **three defects the earlier
session's commits carried** (below), all repaired before any deploy —
and the DEPLOY verification then caught a FOURTH (§6: the premium's
venue drift, exposed by the flip's own acceptance check):

1. **The I11 ECB-leg conversion** (`derived.ts`): the Frankfurter EUR
   leg serves USD→EUR (euros per dollar), so the ECB's EUR millions
   **DIVIDE** by that rate to reach USD millions (€9.53tn ÷ 0.926-ish ≈
   $10.3tn… the live aggregate's own legs: 6.75 + ~10.4 + ~4.4 ≈
   $21.55tn ✓) — the first cut multiplied. No stored data carries the
   wrong leg (no GF-S11 backfill ran; the derivation fires only in the
   worker's rung phases — the deploy lands the fix first).
2. **The F15 PDF extractor** (`sge-monthly.ts`): the committed extractor
   was BROKEN against the very venue it claimed to read —
   `scanPdfObjects`'s dataStart double-counted the object's own file
   offset (an absolute index plus `at`), slicing every stream from deep
   inside its own bytes (the CMap inflates threw bare TypeErrors —
   Node's DecompressionStream surfaces zlib failures as empty-message
   TypeErrors); and the Gold/Silver column-order pin demanded exactly
   one space where the venue's own PDF renders three. **The earlier
   session's "Oct 2026 read live: 92.08 t" claim predates the final
   edit that broke it — the adapter carried NO test, so the gates
   stayed green over the defect.** The repair: the chunk-relative cut +
   the whitespace-tolerant pin; **the extractor gains 12 test suites**
   (a SYNTHETIC venue-shaped PDF built in-test with Node's own zlib —
   the venue's file never enters the repo, the licence stays clean),
   pinning the stream-offset regression, both CMap kinds, the EOL
   tolerance, the three-space header and every fail-closed mutation.
   The live read after the repair: **2026-10 = 92.08 t** (the same
   number — now actually from this session's own run).
3. **The I11 display verdict** (`sources.ts`): the earlier session's
   comment claimed the ECB leg's terms were "unknown → fail-closed",
   keeping the card private — **that never matched the register**: the
   `ecb` row has been `publicDisplayOk: 'yes'` since 2026-10-21 (the
   quoted ECB website terms — the affirmative free-use grant with
   accurate reproduction + citation + stated derivations; the same row
   governing the public DFR/AAA-10y/HICP cards off the same data-api
   host). The generated hidden set agrees (global-liquidity NOT
   hidden). The comment now records the verified verdict trail
   (every leg 'yes': WALCL public-domain · ecb quoted-terms ·
   JPNASSETS citation-required © Bank of Japan · frankfurter yes), the
   card serves PUBLIC with the derivation stated in its whatItIs copy
   and the attribution rendered. **The Data Portal's own terms page is
   unreachable from the build sandbox (NXDOMAIN — a sandbox limit,
   recorded); the quoted website terms are the governing grant on
   file.** If the owner prefers the stricter reading, one owner round
   can flip the row — the mechanism is the register.
